title: Economic Impact of Category Captaincy: An Examination of Assortments and Prices
eligible_reason: Structural (moment-inequality) paper. The only DiD-style reduced-form analyses (Tables A6, 6) use one chain that switched from captaincy to retailer management and two chains that switched captain, with tiny samples (n = 68 and 515) and brand-level triple interactions (Captain's Products x Treated x Treatment).
design_notes: Main identification is a structural model of assortment, pricing and captain selection (Table 7 inequality estimates). Descriptive/reduced-form Tables 2-5 and A1 (chain FE + time FE regression of sales/assortment on captaincy status) are not event-timing designs: 24 chains observed mostly under one arrangement; only one chain moved from no-captaincy to captaincy. Table 6 Scenario 1: single region, 2 chains, one switches (single date). Scenario 2: three regions, two chains switch from the same manufacturer to another (captain identity change, not a binary on/off treatment), regression includes interaction with captain's products.
estimators_reported: OLS reduced-form regressions with brand/region/time dummies (Table 6)
chain and time FE regression (Table A1)
screener_notes: Not eligible: structural paper; auxiliary DiD has one or two switching chains, subgroup/triple interactions, no staggered binary adoption. No replication package was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only. Data: Nielsen Storeview store-week data plus a national food manufacturer's captaincy records (licensed/proprietary).
